### The gate

Round 13 first observed that `TestDocsNextActionRangeIsCurrent` cannot catch this
class: it fires only on literal `a..b` ranges in `status_documents`, while these
counts live in prose. Rounds 14 through 18 each re-derived that same conclusion
from a fresh failure. The remedy is now built rather than noted.

`internal/doccheck/remediation_count_test.go` counts the remediation commits after
the rejected candidate from the git history, derives the applied, review and
outstanding figures from them, and asserts them in **every document that carries a
`Stage 6.3 review state:` line**. Each document must carry exactly one such line and
must state all three figures correctly, so coverage is *required* rather than
attempted: a document that stops carrying the line fails instead of being skipped,
which is the gap round 23 found in the previous version that claimed this same
coverage. It also asserts the pending row names no commit and does name the
outstanding ordinal, and that the rounds table carries exactly one row per review
plus one.

This is the first finding in this stage closed by a mechanism rather than by
care. The four consecutive remediation rounds before it (15–18) were prose
discipline over the same sentence, and none of them managed it.

**What the gate does not check, stated so it is not over-trusted.** It verifies
countable claims against the commit history, in all five documents that carry a
state line. It does **not**:

- **See prose it cannot derive a number from.** R18F2 and R18F3 were earlier
  remediations editing this record's past finding and section text so the numbers
  would agree. That limit was verified, not assumed, and the first version of the
  claim was wrong: it named the experiment "mutating R16F1's text back to
  six/sixth", which is a no-op because R16F1 already reads six/sixth. The
  experiment that establishes it is committing an edit of R16F1's finding text and
  resolution cell — from "six/sixth" to "seven/seventh" — with a clean tree and
  every live count correct, and observing the gate pass. Round 19 ran it and
  confirmed the gate passes there; round 21 swept the whole range and confirmed
  every historical edit is now disclosed.
- **Check prose.** The state line is the machine-checked claim; the count restated
  in prose around it is commentary, and a wrong figure there is not caught. Round 23
  showed the earlier whole-file scan could be satisfied by a table row while the real
  figure was wrong, which is why the state line replaced it — and the cost of that
  is that the other restatements are unchecked.
- **Read the state line's position or indentation.** Any top-level line opening with
  the marker is accepted, so a line nested under a bullet, or placed in a footer
  where no reader of that document would see it, passes. Round 24 noted this; it is
  recorded rather than fixed, because tightening it risks failing an edit that
  changed nothing.
- **Survive the state line being rewrapped.** It is a single line by design, because
  a pattern spanning prose broke on rewrapping — but that relocated the fragility
  onto a line that must not be wrapped, in a repository that wraps everything else.
- **Reach past ninety-nine.** English has no ordinal for a round hundred, the
  helper naming the expected spelling emits digits there, and the state-line
  patterns read letters — so at a hundredth remediation the gate would report that
  the document "states no such claim". It fails closed and loudly, and the stage
  will close long before then, but "no ceiling" is a claim about the *reading*, not
  about every count the record might one day carry.
- **Read only the first number in a pending row's scope cell.** `stage63ReadNumber`
  returns the first parseable token, so a scope reading "the one hundred and first
  remediation" resolves to 1. Unreachable below a hundred, fails closed, and stated
  here because round 22 raised the absence of this line and round 23 found it still
  absent.
- **Survive a renamed section heading, but only while the bound string occurs
  once.** Round 21 renamed a bound heading and the scope silently widened to the
  whole document, at which point the gate read a historical quote as the live count.
  It used to fail closed on a missing bound, by reporting that the header "states no
  such claim". **That assertion was deleted** when the header stopped restating the
  ordinal, so a renamed bound heading is now invisible rather than fail-closed — a
  regression this commit introduced and did not record. The precondition that made
  the old behaviour necessary no longer applies to the header, because the header no
  longer carries a figure.

Each of these still needs a reviewer. A gate reduces a class of defect; it does
not replace the reading.

**Eight remediations exist for round 18, and the reason is the gate's own
history.** `879b435` carried the round-18 fixes and the gate; `52f3d29` fixed two
defects in that gate; `aab834e` corrected the invariant it had falsified and
spelled the counts for the commit it became; `a19fb64` inverted the gate's commit
classification after it under-counted the commit that introduced it; `3b1f959`
recorded that sequence and spelled the count for the commit it became;
`4ea6da3`, `29c5168` and `41423b0` spelled it for theirs. All eight answer
round 18 and all eight are counted, because squashing them would mean rewriting history this
branch has already published.

The loop ended by fixing the gate rather than the number. Its assertion was that
the record's count equals the history count — which is unachievable while
authoring, because the commit carrying the corrected count is itself the next
one. It now accepts the history count **or** one more, and only while the working
tree carries an uncommitted change. The tolerance is one, and it is conditional
on there being something to commit, which is what keeps it from becoming the
off-by-one it was written to prevent.

That sequence is worth stating plainly rather than hiding: **each fix was a new
commit, and each new commit was the thing the gate then caught.** It is the
clearest possible demonstration of the loop this gate exists to close, and of why
closing it needed a mechanism rather than care.

**The gate was verified by mutation, not by reading.** Setting the applied count
to a number the history does not support fails it; setting it to the number the
history does support passes. The same mutation against R16F1's finding text is
invisible to it, which is the limitation stated above rather than a guess.

**Defects in the gate itself, each found by the gate failing on the commit that
introduced or extended it** — which is the only evidence that a gate like this works. It
compared a cardinal against an ordinal, so `ten remediations applied` was
reported as needing to read `tenth`. It assumed exactly one review per
remediation, which its own existence falsified. It classified commits by
enumerating remediation subject prefixes, so the commit that introduced the gate
was not itself counted — a whitelist of inclusions that failed toward
under-counting the thing it measures. And it compared number *words*, so it could
only reach twenty; the twenty-first commit after the candidate would have broken it
for good, and archiving this record would have turned it red permanently. Round 19
found that last one, and noted that at that time the gate was scoped to this one
file while four other documents carried the same count unchecked — which rounds 23
and 24 each then had to fix. The classification is now inverted: every
commit after the rejected candidate counts except three named bookkeeping
commits, because a closed list of exclusions fails toward the opposite, safer
error than a list that must be extended before it sees a new subject.
